independent_methods.division: Python arbitrary-precision divmod with canonical remainder; does not call JavaScript mod
independent_methods.gcd_inverse: Python math.gcd, direct original-input coefficient substitution and exhaustive inverse candidate sets for small moduli
independent_methods.powers: Python three-argument pow; trace factors independently computed as pow(a,2^i,n), accumulator invariants and complete small-period sequence enumeration
independent_methods.factorization: Enumerate prime divisors of the original integer with all possible small divisor certificates, independently of shrinking odd-only runtime trial division
independent_methods.totient_theorems: Complete Python gcd-based unit sets and direct modular powers, with separate checks of the theorem application text
independent_methods.rsa: Python pow and public-only integer factor sets for six keys; exhaustive messages and working private exponent recovery
independent_methods.geometry: Inspect actual emitted sphere/line points; reconstruct per-field stable categories and expected row/field/slot coordinates without trusting adapter panel coordinates
independent_methods.dom: Execute render against an instrumented DOM and compare actual caption/header/body cells, ledgers, controls and speech with independently checked models
independent_methods.input_gate: Execute actual shared spatial runtime in isolated vm instances with controlled scenes; observe actual input type and post-commit value type, rather than source-string assertions

representation_boundaries: Only first40 rows per3D table are drawn; total/visible/omitted counts agree, full companion tables and exact ledger retain the calculations.
Only first64 positive totient representatives are diagrammed; the full unit list is retained and independently checked.
Categorical row/field/value-slot coordinates are layout indices, not integer magnitude, distance or cryptographic difficulty.
Trial factorization is exact only within its stated2..1000000 helper bound; theorem/totient UI bounds are2..10000.
The toy permits prime2 and exponents beyond the RFC public-key range for elementary round-trip arithmetic; it is not an RFC-conformance or secure-key validator.
Infinite theorem proofs were read for quantified logic and hypotheses; finite tests do not establish these theorems or security.
